title: Zuno OKF profile 1.0: task document
description: Frontmatter of tasks/<task>.md of an agent or an experience client in a Zuno OKF profile 1.0 bundle: the upstream Open Knowledge Format 0.2 envelope (https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/open-knowledge-format/blob/main/SPEC.md) plus the namespaced `zuno` block. Frozen (zuno-demo ADR-0615): a change needs a new profile version.

okf_version.description: [OKF] Version of the upstream Open Knowledge Format this document follows (SPEC §12): always the quoted string "0.2". Repeated in every document so a reader can dispatch one file at a time (a declared deviation: upstream declares it once, in the bundle-root index.md).

type.description: [OKF] Document kind (SPEC §4): always "task" in this schema.

resource.description: [OKF] Canonical URI of this document (SPEC §4): its file on the main branch of the repository that publishes it.

sources.description: [OKF] What the document was derived from (SPEC §5 provenance). Descriptive, never a grant: the tasks' declarations are the authorization surface.

generated.description: [OKF] How the content was produced (SPEC §5 trust): an actor (`human:<id>`, `process:<id>` or `<producer>/<version>`) and an instant.

verified.description: [OKF] Independent confirmations (SPEC §5 trust). Absent or empty: unverified; machine actors only: machine-confirmed; a `human:` actor: human-reviewed. Advisory, never a grant. Always a list (a declared deviation: upstream also tolerates a bare mapping).

status.description: [OKF] Lifecycle of the document (SPEC §5): absent means stable. For an agent it agrees with zuno.status: draft for placeholder, stable for active, deprecated for deprecated or retired.

stale_after.description: [OKF] Instant after which the content should be reviewed again (SPEC §5), with an offset.

zuno.description: [ZUNO EXT] Tool-authorization and knowledge-authorization declarations for this task.

profile.description: [ZUNO] Version of the Zuno OKF profile this document follows: always the quoted string "1.0" (zuno-demo ADR-0615).

allowed_tools.description: MCP tool names this task may invoke, drawn from the platform tool-policy vocabulary (policies/tools/README.md). Effective authorization is the intersection of this list with the user's group/task/data-classification policy (ADR-0011) - this field is a ceiling, not a grant on its own. Empty for placeholder agents' stub tasks. A task can only ever narrow, never widen, its parent agent's overall declared-tools union (ADR-0036 Security considerations). The vocabulary itself is policies/tools/tool-policy.yaml, checked by platform/supply-chain/validate_okf_bundle.py; this schema only constrains the name format, so a new tool is declared in one place.

live_read_tool.description: The single entry of allowed_tools that the workflow's live-read branch invokes. Explicit configuration, never derived from caller data; omit it when the task never reads live.

quota_class.description: Named quota class of policies/quotas/quota-policy.yaml; absent means `standard`.

project_required.description: The task needs a verified project id as session context before any tool call, retrieval or model call.

max_tokens.description: Generation ceiling of the task's model call; `zuno.limits.max_tokens` is the preferred placement.

allowed_knowledge.description: Knowledge domain ids (`knowledge.<domain>`) of policies/knowledge/knowledge-policy.yaml the task may retrieve from; independent of allowed_tools.

prompts.description: Extra prompt slots of a multi-stage task: slot name to settings. Each slot's text is prompts/<task>--<slot>.md.

prompt_examples.description: ADR-0515/WP-061: editable example prompts for this task, surfaced in two places by the agent frontend - the empty-state ("Create new chat") view when the caller has no conversation history yet, and the composer's slash menu, which lists every task carrying at least one example and drops the chosen text into the message box for the user to edit before sending. UX only - purely decorative, never parsed/enforced server-side, and choosing one does NOT select which task runs: the chat route always executes the agent's primary_task (ADR-0342). Optional/omitted simply drops this task from the slash menu.

skills.description: ADR-0579 clause 1: skills whose instructions are appended to this task's system prompt, in order. `<name>` is agents/<agent>/skills/<name>.md; `corp/<name>` is policies/skills/<name>.md, shipped with the corp policies.

models.description: ADR-0579 clause 2: model preferences by architectural ROLE (policies/models/model-catalog.yaml `role`), never by model name. The ai-gateway keeps the final choice among the models eligible for the effective classification.

preferred.description: Roles to try first, in order.

limits.description: ADR-0579 clause 4: per-agent (or per-task) bounds, each at most the corp ceiling in policies/limits/limits-policy.yaml.

max_tokens.description: Generation ceiling per model call (ADR-0544); the task-level zuno.max_tokens stays valid as an alias.

max_concurrent_requests.description: Concurrent requests one user may have open on this agent.

max_steps.description: Maximum reasoning/tool rounds of one agent turn; the agent then gives a final answer from what it gathered. At most the corp ceiling max_steps (policies/limits/limits-policy.yaml). A task-level value overrides the agent's. Absent: the runtime default (unifai-operator: 15).

max_tokens_per_turn.description: Maximum model tokens one agent turn may use (one user submit, all model calls of the turn). The turn ends cleanly when the ceiling is reached: the last text the model produced, a blank line and the notice "Token ceiling reached for this turn (<used>/<cap> tokens)". The cap is checked between model calls, so the last call can exceed it. At most the corp ceiling max_tokens_per_turn when the corp policy sets one (policies/limits/limits-policy.yaml). A task-level value overrides the agent's. Absent: no ceiling (today's behaviour). Needs unifai-operator 0.1.65 or later.
